system.name: X-Pruner
system.one_liner: Explainable pruning of vision transformers: class-wise explainability-aware masks are learned per prunable unit and used to choose which units to prune.

content.variant_note: the method drawn in tensor notation: offset stacks of 5 by 5 cell grids for weights, class masks and activations, with translucent cones for multiplication and pruning, in a Training panel and a Testing panel
content.argues: Class-wise explainability-aware masks learned in training are summed over classes into one pruning mask that shrinks W, so pruning follows each unit's relevance to the classes.
content.subject: Weight matrix W with class mask columns in training, and a sum reduction of the masks into a pruning mask that gives Pruned W in testing

content.reading_order: Starts at the W stack and the purple W_ij M label at the top left of Training, goes down the blue cone to the lower stack and along the black arrow to the coloured output stack, then crosses to Testing: sum reduction at the top, the orange cone down to Pruned W and Batch x.

layout.arrangement_note: Two grey-framed panels side by side: Training (about 60% of the width) and Testing, whose frame is split by a horizontal line into an upper and a lower cell. In Training, oblique stacks of grids run from the weights and mask columns at the top left through a blue translucent cone to the lower stack, and a black arrow leads to the coloured output stack; in Testing the masks are reduced to one orange column, an orange cone narrows W to Pruned W, and the Batch x grid sits beside it. The phase names are bold words at the foot of each panel.

summary: X-Pruner is an explainable pruning framework for vision transformers that learns class-wise explainability-aware masks for the prunable units of a layer and prunes with them. Figure 1 is a tensor-level diagram in two framed panels. In Training, a stack of weight matrices W, each paired with the mask column of its sample's class (picked from four class columns by the label y_k), leads through a blue cone to a class-tinted stack that is multiplied with the layer input x to give the next layer's output, with one colour per class throughout. In Testing, the class masks are reduced by a sum to one orange column, an orange cone narrows W to Pruned W, and a Batch x grid sits beside it. All items are cell grids; there is no sample data.
summary_zh: X-Pruner 为视觉 Transformer 学习按类别区分的掩码来剪枝。图用矩阵切片堆叠画法分两栏：训练栏中权重 W 乘以按标签选出的类别掩码列；测试栏把各类掩码求和成一列橙色剪枝掩码，把 W 剪成 Pruned W。
notes: The index calls this chart/bar (pgfplots metadata); it is a tensor-notation diagram, not a chart. No paragraph mentions the figure: the reading of the six-slice stacks as one slice per sample with its class colour, of the white gaps and of the cones is inferred from the labels (W_ij M:,y_k, Indexed by y_k, Sum reduction, Matrix multiplication, Pruning) and may not match the authors' exact intent.
